html:
The Sakalava kingdoms of Menabe and Boina were states on the west coast of Madagascar, founded in the 17th century by the Maroserana dynasty and for a time the strongest powers on the island.

They grew rich by trading cattle and captives with European, Swahili and Arab ships for guns, and their armies raided far inland. Royal relics of dead kings, kept and honoured in a ceremony still held today, were the heart of their rule.

In the 19th century the Merina kingdom of the highlands, armed by Britain under Radama I, conquered much of their land, though the Sakalava resisted for decades. They remain one of the largest groups of Madagascar, and their ports traded with the pirates of Sainte-Marie and the Comoros.
